raw_response:
I farm only 8 mu, so I cannot take big risks. Same as most people here, I will keep the wheat-maize rotation. Wheat still gives steady grain, and maize follows right after, so even if one side is not perfect, the whole year is still safer. I have done this many years, and with some family members working outside, I need a plan that does not need too much hired labor or too much cash all at once.

For wheat, I will sow in early October, about the usual village time. I do not want to plant too late, because then the seedlings are weak before winter. I will use a common improved variety that people around here can buy easily. Fertilizer, I will not cut too much. If wheat turns yellow, it is hard to recover yield, so I would rather put a fair base fertilizer and then topdress once in spring. Water costs money from the well, so I will not irrigate too many times, but I will still give wheat 3 irrigations if the rain is not enough, because wheat here usually needs that.

For maize, I will plant as soon as wheat is harvested in June. The turnaround is tight, so I will keep it simple, with light rotary tillage or direct sowing after the wheat comes off. I will use hybrid maize seed, because local saved maize seed is not as reliable for yield. I will put fertilizer in two times, one at sowing and one around jointing, roughly like what I did before and what neighbors do. If rain is normal, I may irrigate once or twice, not more. I will watch weeds and corn borer, and spray only if I really see the problem getting serious. This year I want steady yield, not fancy changes.
